source.title: Bilateral Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Flatter Minima
source.authors: Jia-Xin Deng; Jun-Biao Pang; Bao-Chang Zhang; Qing-Ming Huang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices. The arXiv version date and cited works appear inconsistent with the stated venue/year, but the document is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares a new sharpness-based optimizer with SAM and SGD, measures Hessian eigenvalues as a flatness proxy, and reports test accuracy across multiple settings. These results bear on V7's relation between a flatness measure and generalization, using a different measure and method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for BSAM, SAM and SGD on test accuracy and Hessian eigenvalues, and reports sensitivity to MinS radius and label noise. Cited results about prior work, including claims about SAM, are not extracted as this study's own results. Rows focus on V7; the other claim versions are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study uses sharpness minimization to develop BSAM and evaluates optimizer performance. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware weight-perturbation measure against train-test gaps or competing generalization measures. Test-set Hessian spectra measure a different construct, and the remaining experiments test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record fairly paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they claim bilateral sharpness produces flatter minima, improves generalization across tasks and increases robustness to label noise. Their claimed curvature improvement over SAM conflicts with the recorded Figure 5 numbers. Their theorem establishes conditional first-order stationarity, not flatter minima or a generalization guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: BSAM adds a minimum-side gradient perturbation and a decaying MinS radius to SAM, and compares it with SAM and SGD rather than reproducing the original generalization-gap studies.
record.method_sensitivity: MinS radius changes test accuracy; the effects differ between CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Label-noise rate changes test accuracy and the relative optimizer results.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM and BSAM have smaller test-set Hessian eigenvalues than SGD on ResNet-18/CIFAR-100. The recorded numbers place SAM below BSAM, despite the prose claiming the reverse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-aware optimizers can reduce unscaled test-loss Hessian curvature relative to SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: BSAM has higher test accuracy than SGD and SAM at every reported label-noise rate on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BSAM improves held-out classification accuracy under symmetric training-label noise relative to the tested SGD and SAM recipes.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: For the V7-specific comparison, the Hessian eigenvalue analysis is limited to ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 and does not report train-test gaps or matched training loss. The paper itself notes that its convergence theorem does not establish a comparison of Hessian eigenvalues with SAM. Label-noise experiments report test accuracy but not training accuracy or generalization gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Other test-accuracy tables compare optimizers on natural datasets and downstream tasks but do not test any listed version's defining claim; they are not included as version rows.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, with chance held-out performance on random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning. The pose experiment uses Adam as the base optimizer for both SAM and BSAM.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout addition, removal, strength and dependence on dataset size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with train-test gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. Better optimizer accuracy and lower unscaled test-set curvature do not by themselves test V7. The figure/prose discrepancy cannot be resolved confidently from the supplied text extraction.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization alongside generalization on natural labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparisons under tuning constraints.
Large-batch generalization gaps under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout effects and removal of dropout or weight decay.

No magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness measure or comparison of its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. The study compares maximum Hessian eigenvalues for only one architecture and dataset, using CIFAR-100 test data; the paper does not report matched training loss or a training-to-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and comparing retraining with random-example removal.
